dedupe_keys.name: hybrid and cyclic testing of steel moment frames with deep column

description: Hybrid and Cyclic Testing of Steel Moment Frames with Deep Column is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "hybrid simulation", published or maintained by Gilberto Mosqueda, University of California San Diego (ucsd.edu). Steel moment frames composed of wide-flange steel members are commonly used in seismic regions, with deep and slender column sections often selected to economically satisfy drift limit requirements. The section slenderness makes the columns more susceptible to local and global buckling and subsequent axial shortening when subjected to combined high axial forces and lateral deformations. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "hybrid simulation" project. Keywords: Deep columns, steel moment frames, quasi-static, hybrid simulation, full-scale subassembly, reduced beam section. Published 2024-12-26. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
